title: पञ्चाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 285 · Janaka asks how the orders arose

summary.en: Janaka asks Parashara how a man comes to be of a particular order, and the sage tells how the sons of one father came to be of different orders and how a shudra does not fall by birth alone. He says that all orders who rightly do their duties, speak the truth and give up cruelty reach heaven, with no doubt.
summary.kn: ಮನುಷ್ಯ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ವರ್ಣ ಹೇಗೆ ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆಂದು ಜನಕ ಪರಾಶರನನ್ನು ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಒಬ್ಬ ತಂದೆಯ ಮಕ್ಕಳು ಬೇರೆ ವರ್ಣಗಳಾದುದು, ಜನ್ಮದಿಂದ ಮಾತ್ರ ಶೂದ್ರ ಬೀಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲವೆಂದು ಋಷಿ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಕರ್ತವ್ಯ ಮಾಡಿ, ಸತ್ಯ ಹೇಳಿ, ಕ್ರೂರತೆ ತೊರೆದ ಎಲ್ಲ ವರ್ಣದವರು ಸ್ವರ್ಗ ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: जनक पराशर से पूछते हैं कि मनुष्य किसी विशेष वर्ण का कैसे होता है, और ऋषि बताते हैं कि एक पिता के पुत्र अलग वर्णों के कैसे हुए और शूद्र केवल जन्म से नहीं गिरता। वे कहते हैं कि कर्तव्य ठीक से निभाने, सत्य बोलने और क्रूरता छोड़ने वाले सब वर्ण स्वर्ग जाते हैं, इसमें संशय नहीं।
summary.te: మనిషి ఒక నిర్దిష్ట వర్ణానికి ఎలా చెందుతాడని జనకుడు పరాశరుని అడుగుతాడు; ఒక తండ్రి కుమారులు వేర్వేరు వర్ణాలైన తీరు, శూద్రుడు జన్మతో మాత్రమే పతనం కాడని ఋషి చెబుతాడు. కర్తవ్యాలు సరిగ్గా చేసి సత్యం పలికి క్రూరత్వం విడిచిన అన్ని వర్ణాలవారు స్వర్గం పొందుతారు.
summary.ta: மனிதன் ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட வருணத்தை எவ்வாறு அடைகிறான் என்று ஜனகன் பராசரரைக் கேட்க, ஒரே தந்தையின் மகன்கள் வெவ்வேறு வருணத்தவரான விதத்தையும் சூத்திரன் பிறப்பால் மட்டும் வீழ்வதில்லை என்பதையும் முனிவர் கூறுகிறார். கடமையைச் சரியாகச் செய்து உண்மை பேசிக் கொடுமையைத் துறக்கும் எல்லா வருணத்தாரும் சொர்க்கம் அடைவர் என்கிறார்.
summary.ml: ഒരാൾ ഒരു വർണ്ണത്തിൽ പെടുന്നതെങ്ങനെയെന്ന് ജനകൻ പരാശരനോട് ചോദിക്കുന്നു; ഒരേ പിതാവിന്റെ പുത്രന്മാർ വ്യത്യസ്ത വർണ്ണങ്ങളിലായതും, ജന്മം മാത്രംകൊണ്ട് ശൂദ്രൻ വീഴുന്നില്ലെന്നതും മുനി വിവരിക്കുന്നു. കടമകൾ ശരിയായി ചെയ്യുകയും സത്യം പറയുകയും ക്രൂരത ഉപേക്ഷിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്ന എല്ലാ വർണ്ണക്കാരും സ്വർഗ്ഗം പ്രാപിക്കുമെന്ന് സംശയമില്ലാതെ അദ്ദേഹം പറയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.285; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: जनक उवाच

meaning.en: Janaka said:

verses.text:
वर्णो विशेषवर्णानां महर्षे केन जायते ।
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तद्ब्रूहि वदतां वर ॥

meaning.en: Great sage, how do the distinct classes come to have their particular class? I wish to hear this; tell it, best of speakers.

verses.text:
यदेतज्जायतेऽपत्यं स एवायमिति श्रुतिः ।
कथं ब्राह्मणतो जातो विशेषग्रहणं गतः ॥

meaning.en: Scripture says that the offspring who is born is the same as the one who begets. How then does one born of a Brahmin come to take a different class?

verses.text: पराशर उवाच

meaning.en: Parashara said:

verses.text:
एवमेतन्महाराज येन जातः स एव सः ।
तपसस्त्वपकर्षेण जातिग्रहणतां गतः ॥

meaning.en: It is so, great king; he is the same as the one by whom he was born. But through a decline in austerity he comes to be taken as of another birth-class.

verses.text:
सुक्षेत्राच्च सुबीजाच्च पुण्यो भवति संभवः ।
अतोऽन्यतरतो हीनादवरो नाम जायते ॥

meaning.en: From good soil and good seed a pure birth results; from either one being poor, an inferior is born.

verses.text:
वक्त्राद्भुजाभ्यामूरुभ्यां पद्भ्यां चैवाथ जज्ञिरे ।
सृजतः प्रजापतेर्लोकानिति धर्मविदो विदुः ॥

meaning.en: Those who know dharma say that, as Prajapati created the worlds, people were born from his mouth, arms, thighs and feet.

verses.text:
मुखजा ब्राह्मणास्तात बाहुजाः क्षत्रबन्धवः ।
ऊरुजा धनिनो राजन्पादजाः परिचारकाः ॥

meaning.en: Dear one, those born of the mouth are Brahmins, those of the arms Kshatriyas, those of the thighs, king, the wealthy, and those of the feet the servants.

verses.text:
चतुर्णामेव वर्णानामागमः पुरुषर्षभ ।
अतोऽन्ये त्वतिरिक्ता ये ते वै संकरजाः स्मृताः ॥

meaning.en: Bull among men, the origin is of the four classes only; any others besides these are remembered as born of mixture.

verses.text:
क्षत्रजातिरथाम्बष्ठा उग्रा वैदेहकास्तथा ।
श्वपाकाः पुल्कसाः स्तेना निषादाः सूतमागधाः ॥

meaning.en: They are the Kshatriya-born, the Ambashthas, Ugras, Vaidehakas, Shvapakas, Pulkasas, Stenas, Nishadas, Sutas and Magadhas,

verses.text:
आयोगाः करणा व्रात्याश्चण्डालाश्च नराधिप ।
एते चतुर्भ्यो वर्णेभ्यो जायन्ते वै परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: the Ayogas, Karanas, Vratyas and Chandalas, lord of men; these are born from the four classes by mixing with one another.

verses.text: जनक उवाच

meaning.en: Janaka said:

verses.text:
ब्रह्मणैकेन जातानां नानात्वं गोत्रतः कथम् ।
बहूनीह हि लोके वै गोत्राणि मुनिसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: How is there diversity of lineage among those born of the one Brahma? In this world, best of sages, there are many lineages.

verses.text:
यत्र तत्र कथं जाताः स्वयोनिं मुनयो गताः ।
शूद्रयोनौ समुत्पन्ना वियोनौ च तथापरे ॥

meaning.en: How is it that sages born here and there reached their own station, some born of Shudra wombs and others of non-human wombs?

verses.text: पराशर उवाच

meaning.en: Parashara said:

verses.text:
राजन्नैतद्भवेद्ग्राह्यमपकृष्टेन जन्मना ।
महात्मनां समुत्पत्तिस्तपसा भावितात्मनाम् ॥

meaning.en: King, this should not be judged by lowly birth; the origins of the great-souled, whose selves are purified by austerity, are another matter.

verses.text:
उत्पाद्य पुत्रान्मुनयो नृपते यत्र तत्र ह ।
स्वेनैव तपसा तेषामृषित्वं विदधुः पुनः ॥

meaning.en: Having fathered sons here and there, king, the sages again gave them the rank of sages by their own austerity.

verses.text:
पितामहश्च मे पूर्वमृश्यशृङ्गश्च काश्यपः ।
वटस्ताण्ड्यः कृपश्चैव कक्षीवान्कमठादयः ॥

meaning.en: My grandfather before, and Rishyashringa, Kashyapa, Vata, Tandya, Kripa, Kakshivan, Kamatha and others,

verses.text:
यवक्रीतश्च नृपते द्रोणश्च वदतां वरः ।
आयुर्मतङ्गो दत्तश्च द्रुपदो मत्स्य एव च ॥

meaning.en: and Yavakrita, king, and Drona, best of speakers, Ayu, Matanga, Datta, Drupada and Matsya,

verses.text:
एते स्वां प्रकृतिं प्राप्ता वैदेह तपसोऽऽश्रयात् ।
प्रतिष्ठिता वेदविदो दमे तपसि चैव हि ॥

meaning.en: these, Videha, reached their own true nature by resorting to austerity. They became established in the Vedas, in self-control and in austerity.

verses.text:
मूलगोत्राणि चत्वारि समुत्पन्नानि पार्थिव ।
अङ्गिराः कश्यपश्चैव वसिष्ठो भृगुरेव च ॥

meaning.en: Four root lineages have arisen, king: Angiras, Kashyapa, Vasishtha and Bhrigu.

verses.text:
कर्मतोऽन्यानि गोत्राणि समुत्पन्नानि पार्थिव ।
नामधेयानि तपसा तानि च ग्रहणं सताम् ॥

meaning.en: Other lineages have arisen from action, king; those names are adopted by the good through austerity.

verses.text: जनक उवाच

meaning.en: Janaka said:

verses.text:
विशेषधर्मान्वर्णानां प्रब्रूहि भगवन्मम ।
तथा सामान्यधर्मांश्च सर्वत्र कुशलो ह्यसि ॥

meaning.en: Revered sir, tell me the special duties of the classes, and also the common duties; for you are skilled in everything.

verses.text: पराशर उवाच

meaning.en: Parashara said:

verses.text:
प्रतिग्रहो याजनं च तथैवाध्यापनं नृप ।
विशेषधर्मो विप्राणां रक्षा क्षत्रस्य शोभना ॥

meaning.en: Accepting gifts, performing sacrifices for others, and teaching, king, are the special duties of Brahmins; protection is the fine duty of the Kshatriya.

verses.text:
कृषिश्च पाशुपाल्यं च वाणिज्यं च विशामपि ।
द्विजानां परिचर्या च शूद्रकर्म नराधिप ॥

meaning.en: Farming, cattle-keeping and trade belong to the Vaishyas; and serving the twice-born is the work of the Shudra, lord of men.

verses.text:
विशेषधर्मा नृपते वर्णानां परिकीर्तिताः ।
धर्मान्साधारणांस्तात विस्तरेण शृणुष्व मे ॥

meaning.en: King, the special duties of the classes have been declared. Now hear from me at length the common duties, dear one.

verses.text:
आनृशंस्यमहिंसा चाप्रमादः संविभागिता ।
श्राद्धकर्मातिथेयं च सत्यमक्रोध एव च ॥

meaning.en: Kindness, nonviolence, vigilance, sharing, rites for the ancestors, hospitality, truthfulness and freedom from anger,

verses.text:
स्वेषु दारेषु संतोषः शौचं नित्यानसूयता ।
आत्मज्ञानं तितिक्षा च धर्माः साधारणा नृप ॥

meaning.en: contentment with one's own wives, purity, constant freedom from envy, knowledge of the self and patience: these are the common duties, king.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्यास्त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः ।
अत्र तेषामधीकारो धर्मेषु द्विपदां वर ॥

meaning.en: Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas are the three twice-born classes, and they have authority over these duties, best of men.

verses.text:
विकर्मावस्थिता वर्णाः पतन्ति नृपते त्रयः ।
उन्नमन्ति यथासन्तमाश्रित्येह स्वकर्मसु ॥

meaning.en: The three classes, king, fall when they are engaged in wrong action; and they rise up by resorting to the good in their own duties.

verses.text:
न चापि शूद्रः पततीति निश्चयो
न चापि संस्कारमिहार्हतीति वा ।
श्रुतिप्रवृत्तं न च धर्ममाप्नुते
न चास्य धर्मे प्रतिषेधनं कृतम् ॥

meaning.en: It is settled that a Shudra does not fall, nor does he deserve the sacramental rites here; he does not obtain the dharma that stems from the Veda, yet no prohibition has been made against his following dharma.

verses.text:
वैदेहकं शूद्रमुदाहरन्ति
द्विजा महाराज श्रुतोपपन्नाः ।
अहं हि पश्यामि नरेन्द्र देवं
विश्वस्य विष्णुं जगतः प्रधानम् ॥

meaning.en: The learned twice-born, great king, cite a Vaidehaka as an example of a Shudra. I indeed see, lord of men, Vishnu, the god, the chief of the whole world.

verses.text:
सतां वृत्तमनुष्ठाय निहीना उज्जिहीर्षवः ।
मन्त्रवर्जं न दुष्यन्ति कुर्वाणाः पौष्टिकीः क्रियाः ॥

meaning.en: The lowly who wish to raise themselves, by following the conduct of the good and doing rites for prosperity without mantras, are not at fault.

verses.text:
यथा यथा हि सद्वृत्तमालम्बन्तीतरे जनाः ।
तथा तथा सुखं प्राप्य प्रेत्य चेह च शेरते ॥

meaning.en: As other people increasingly take up good conduct, so they gain happiness here and hereafter and rest in it.

verses.text: जनक उवाच

meaning.en: Janaka said:

verses.text:
किं कर्म दूषयत्येनमथ जातिर्महामुने ।
संदेहो मे समुत्पन्नस्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥

meaning.en: Great sage, what corrupts a man: his action or his birth? A doubt has arisen in me; please explain it to me.

verses.text: पराशर उवाच

meaning.en: Parashara said:

verses.text:
असंशयं महाराज उभयं दोषकारकम् ।
कर्म चैव हि जातिश्च विशेषं तु निशामय ॥

meaning.en: Without doubt, great king, both can be causes of fault, action and birth. But hear the difference.

verses.text:
जात्या च कर्मणा चैव दुष्टं कर्म निषेवते ।
जात्या दुष्टश्च यः पापं न करोति स पूरुषः ॥

meaning.en: He who is corrupt by birth and by action follows corrupt action; but the man who is corrupt by birth and yet does not commit sin is a true man.

verses.text:
जात्या प्रधानं पुरुषं कुर्वाणं कर्म धिक्कृतम् ।
कर्म तद्दूषयत्येनं तस्मात्कर्म नशोभनम् ॥

meaning.en: When a man high by birth does a deed that is condemned, that action corrupts him; therefore such action is not good.

verses.text: जनक उवाच

meaning.en: Janaka said:

verses.text:
कानि कर्माणि धर्म्याणि लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विजसत्तम ।
न हिंसन्तीह भूतानि क्रियमाणानि सर्वदा ॥

meaning.en: Best of the twice-born, which actions in this world are righteous and, when done, never injure beings?

verses.text: पराशर उवाच

meaning.en: Parashara said:

verses.text:
शृणु मेऽत्र महाराज यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ।
यानि कर्माण्यहिंस्राणि नरं त्रायन्ति सर्वदा ॥

meaning.en: Hear from me here, great king, what you ask me: which actions free of violence always protect a man.

verses.text:
संन्यस्याग्नीनुपासीनाः पश्यन्ति विगतज्वराः ।
नैःश्रेयसं धर्मपथं समारुह्य यथाक्रमम् ॥

meaning.en: Those who have given up the sacrificial fires, who sit in meditation and are free of fever, see; having climbed the path of dharma that leads to the highest good in due order,

verses.text:
प्रश्रिता विनयोपेता दमनित्याः सुसंशिताः ।
प्रयान्ति स्थानमजरं सर्वकर्मविवर्जिताः ॥

meaning.en: humble, well-mannered, constant in self-control and sharp of mind, they go to the changeless state, free of all action.

verses.text:
सर्वे वर्णा धर्मकार्याणि सम्य-
क्कृत्वा राजन्सत्यवाक्यानि चोक्त्वा ।
त्यक्त्वाधर्मं दारुणं जीवलोके
यान्ति स्वर्गं नात्र कार्यो विचारः ॥

meaning.en: When all classes have properly done the works of dharma and spoken truthful words, king, and given up the cruel adharma of the living world, they go to heaven; on this there is nothing to ponder.
